page.running_head: Sect. I. Part. I. Cap. XXI.

main_text.l: Scaliger, exerc.22 5.sect. 3.Primum visibile lux est: reliqua omnia, ut actu videantur, luce indigent.Vide Patricium lib.2.Panaugiæ.
Finis cum effectu concurrit: quia est lumen per illuminationem productum.
In explicatione adjunctorum lucis effecta quoq; nonnulla obiter attingentur.
Lumen est fulgor à luce undiquaque emanans: aliis, actus perspicui.

I. Luminis naturam ex sententiâ suâ explicat Pa-tricius, lib. 4. Panaugiæ: ubi (1) ostendit lumen immediatè non esse à luce, sed à radio: & hanc causam esse ait, quod lumen minus fulgeat, quàm radius: quia in primo gradu lux, in secundo radius, in tertio lumen.(2)Radii & luminis multiplicem convenientiam explicat: (3)propria luminis prolixè persequitur: Ex sententia autem Patricii lumen nulli rei miscetur, nec cognatis quidem luminibus: nullis sordibus inquinatur: maximo sui amplificandi desiderio tenetur: figuram orbicularem amat: in progressu debilitatur: minus à majori oculitur: reflectitur & refringitur: virtutum cœlestium est vehiculum & vin-

page.notes: The Greek headings read as Ἔκθεσις (exposition), marked [?] because the letters are small. The signature "Pp 5" is uncertain. The text breaks off at "vin-" and continues on the next page. Long s is plain s throughout; the "ff" ligatures are kept as printed.
